translation:
Viewed from this, the five viscera and six bowels, the four limbs and hundred bones, all receive from the Spleen and Stomach, which transport their fluids, mutually moistening and nourishing them. How could later physicians, wishing to nourish the Spleen and Stomach and enrich the qi of earth with drying-heat formulas, not be in error! Moreover, in the disease of wasting-thirst (消渴), the yin qi of dampness-cold is extremely weakened and the yang qi of dryness-heat is excessive; if one further administers drying-heat medicines, then the qi of the Spleen and Stomach is exhausted.

The later generations do not distinguish the vacuity and repletion of the five movements and six qi, but uniformly say that heat is repletion and vacuity is cold. They only know the vacuity and repletion of the single qi of heart-fire yang-heat, and not the vacuity and repletion of the six qi of the viscera and bowels.
translator_notes: 消渴 rendered as wasting-thirst (standard English term).
五運六氣 rendered as five movements and six qi.
